text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's caretaker cabinet liberalised prices on goods in line with pledges to the International Monetary Fund to speed up economic reforms. Controls remain in force for nine basic items.

-- Bulgaria's Union of Democratic Forces (UDF), which won a big parliamentary majority in Saturday's general election, is expected on Thursday to nominate its leader Ivan Kostov as prime minister and decide on the makeup of the new UDF cabinet.
-- The UDF will meet leaders of the other parties represented in the new parliament to seek their support for a programme to end the country's economic crisis, UDF leader Ivan Kostov said.

Kostov said UDF priorities were implementing economic reforms agreed with multilateral lenders, fighting organised crime, opening secret police files of politicians and bringing the country into the European Union and NATO.
-- Thousands of UDF supporters gathered despite the rain in central Sofia at a rally to celebrate the UDF victory in Saturday's election.
The electoral commission said the UDF and its allies had 137 seats in the 240-seat National Assembly and gave the former ruling Socialists 57 seats.
-- Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) foreign exchange reserves rose to $1.09 billion on April 21 from $554.3 million on March 31, the BNB said.
-- The sales of the cement plants Zlatna Panega and Granitoid Batanovtsi are expected to be finalised in the first half of May, the construction ministry said.
-- The UDF will seek the opening of secret police files of members of parliament, cabinet members and supreme court judges, its leader Ivan Kostov said.

-- The leaders of the former ruling Socialist Party said they would respond to the UDF appeal for cooperation in the anti-crisis programme and planned to meet UDF leader Ivan Kostov for talks on Tuesday.
